page.layout: One page of text, with the running head and page number at the top. No marginal notes. Top: page number "202" at left, running head "CONCIONES" at centre. Then the continuing paragraph from the previous page, a short paragraph, a German black-letter line, the Latin closing sentence, the division heading "CONCIO XXXIIII.", the passage reference "Eccles. 7.", and the opening paragraph with a woodcut initial, which runs on to the next page.

main_text.p: & Eph. 4. Omnis amarulentia, & tumor, & ira, & vociferat o, & maledicentia tollatur à vobis cum omni malitia, &c. Instar leonum vorat, qui corda sua crapula & ebrietate grauant, Luc. 21. ebriosi operarij, Eccles. 19.

ʒ Cæterum quid faciendum est illi, qui vel leoninam naturam habet, vel coniugem, aut principem leoni similem, cuiusmodi fuit Nabal, Herodes, Cambyses, Nero, &c. Orandus Dominus (qui Dauidem, Danielem, Paulum de manu & ore leonum eripuit, 1. Reg. 17. Dan. 6. 2. Tim. 4.) pro spiritu (quo Samson leonem vicit & dilaceravit, Iudic. 14.) idque fide (qua occludi possunt ora leonum, Hebr. 11.) & humili animo. Dann Des grausamen Löwen zorn vnd vbermut / vberwinde[?] das hündlin mit demut. Pater noster cœlestis liberet nos à pessimo illo[?] leone, qui diabolus est, per Christum Iesum, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXXIIII.
Eccles. 7.
main_text.p: Vxore sapiente bonaq; caue ne excidas (si quam secundum religione Domini nactus es:) nam venustas eius praestanti-ar[?] auro est. Ne male tractes famulum operantem fideliter, nec mercenarium sese totum impendentem. Famulum corda-tum

page.notes: Initial "V" is a woodcut letter; read as V with the rest of "xore". "vociferat o" is printed with a space inside the word. Line "praestanti-ar" is unclear at the hyphen; the word is probably "praestantior". "peisimo" and "ilto" are uncertain readings. "vberwinde" in the black-letter line is uncertain. The paragraph mark "ʒ" before "Cæterum" is printed and kept.
